title: elastic-fragmentation-prefill-and-handshake-consolidation-for-reduced-synchronization
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Reduce prefill-decode synchronization overhead and improve tail latency for mixed-length workloads. Large monolithic prefill windows force decode stages to wait for bulk prefill completion; small fixed microchunks underutilize kernels and increase scheduling overhead. This PR introduces an "elastic fragmentation" approach where prefill is split into variable-size fragments aligned to ongoing decode handshakes, and a handshake consolidation path that collapses frequent small synchronization points into fewer coordinated handoffs.

Goals: 1) reduce end-to-end P95/P99 latency for short-to-medium responses, 2) improve GPU kernel utilization for varied sequence-length workloads, 3) lower per-token cost via better batching while preserving SLOs.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Implements fragment-level prefill (fragment_coalescer and fragment_router), an adaptive elastic-window scheduler that tunes fragment sizes based on live latency signals and sequence-length histograms, introduces fragment-aware KV-cache zones with soft-evict hints, and adds a handshake consolidator that aggregates decode readiness signals to minimize mutex churn. Also adds feature flags and a canary rollout plan.

Design details: - Fragmentation: Prefill now emits "fragments" (logical prefill groups) rather than one bulk batch. Each fragment carries a small header (fragment_id, priority_hint, target_kv_zone) consumed by downstream decode handoff. Fragment sizes are adaptive: the elastic-window scheduler picks a target fragment token count based on rolling P50/P95 and the observed distribution of request lengths. - Handshake consolidation: Instead of per-fragment blocking handoffs, we provide a consolidator layer in the pipeline that batches handoff notifications and completes decode trigger events in a single bulk operation when safe. This reduces inter-thread synchronization and atomic operations on the hot path. - Fragment-aware KV-cache: KV cache is partitioned into lightweight zones; fragments declare a target zone so we can preferentially pre-warm and apply soft-evict heuristics that avoid thrashing cross-fragment keys. - Kernel hinting: Added a small kernel selection hint (fragment_coalescer_hint) to prefer kernels optimized for short-prefix reuse when fragment reuse is high. - Backwards compatibility: Old prefill path preserved behind feature flag (enable_elastic_fragments). Default rollout is off; canary enabled for 5% of traffic.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of fragment emitter + scheduler - [x] KV-zone soft-evict logic and metrics - [x] Handshake consolidator with safety invariants - [x] Unit tests for fragment lifecycle - [x] Integration tests (local and CI) - [x] Canary rollout automation and monitoring dashboards - [x] Documentation and API notes for ops flags

Testing & validation: Unit+integration test suite added under runtime/tests/fragments. Ran canary across internal staging cluster for 72h. Observability added: fragment size histogram, fragment-handshake latency, kv-zone hit/miss ratios, consolidated-handshake aggregation counts. CI initially flagged a flaky test (runtime/tests/kvcache/test_zone_eviction) due to timing assumptions; the test was hardened and rerun (CI success).

Perf summary (from staging canary, aggregated across 6 runs): - P50 generation latency: -3.2% (no-regress) - P95 generation latency: -9.8% - P99 generation latency: -12.4% - Throughput (tokens/sec on same GPU fleet): +9.1% - Estimated per-token GPU cost: -4.6% (due to improved batching / fewer small kernel launches) Observed improvements largest on mixed-length workloads (some short + some long).

Rollout plan: Feature flag gated; canary at 5% for 48h -> 25% for 24h -> 100% if metrics stable. Auto-backout triggers on >5% regression in P95 or >1% drop in correctness evals.

Related: This complements but is intentionally different from previous microchunk and prefetch work: fragmentation focuses on adaptive logical grouping plus handshake consolidation rather than fixed microchunk counts or purely speculative prefill.

Merge notes: Squashed and merged after reviewers approved and canary verified.

review_comments: Lena Ortega: Can you enumerate the safety invariants for the consolidator? Need to be sure we never reorder decode-visible tokens. Also request a short race-condition doc.
Priya Shah (author): Added a 'consolidator-safety.md' section to docs and implemented explicit sequence-number checks in handshake_consolidator; pushed commit d4a6bf2 to address this.
Marcus Wei: Why partition KV into zones instead of improving global LRU? Curious about memory amplification.
Priya Shah: Zones are a low-friction heuristic to reduce cross-fragment churn on shared caches; added metrics to watch for amplification and a configuration knob to revert to global LRU per-tenant.
Tobias Singh: CI showed a flaky kvcache test; after hardening it looks stable. Approving on green.

release_notes: Introduce elastic fragment prefill with handshake consolidation and fragment-aware KV zones. Feature gated behind enable_elastic_fragments. Expected tail latency improvements on mixed-length workloads; canary rollout recommended.
